directAnswer: Pope John VII, a Greek and the son of a Byzantine official in Rome, reigned from 705 to 707. He is remembered as a patron of art, especially for his chapel to the Virgin in Old St. Peter's and the frescoes of Santa Maria Antiqua, and for returning Justinian II's Quinisext canons without comment.

sections.h2: The Son of the Palatine's Curator
paras: John was the son of Plato, the official responsible for the imperial palace on the Palatine Hill, and he is the first pope known to have been the son of a Byzantine civil official. He had family ties to the old imperial heart of Rome, and as pope he built an episcopal residence on the Palatine above the church of Santa Maria Antiqua. He was the second pope to take the same name as his immediate predecessor.

sections.h2: Patron of Santa Maria Antiqua and the Oratory of the Virgin
paras: John is best known for his artistic commissions. He built an oratory dedicated to the Mother of God inside Old St. Peter's, decorated with mosaics; fragments survive in the Vatican Grottoes and elsewhere, including a portrait of John holding a model of the chapel. He also had Santa Maria Antiqua, in the Roman Forum, richly painted with frescoes, many of which can still be seen today.

When Justinian II returned to power in 705, he sent the canons of the Quinisext Council to Rome, asking the pope to confirm those he could and reject the rest. The Liber Pontificalis says John, out of human weakness, returned them without changes. He died on 18 October 707 and was buried in his chapel at St. Peter's.

keyFacts: Of Greek origin; son of Plato, curator of the imperial palace on the Palatine
Built an oratory to the Virgin in Old St. Peter's
Commissioned frescoes at Santa Maria Antiqua in the Roman Forum
Returned the Quinisext canons to Justinian II without comment

faqs.question: What art survives from Pope John VII?
faqs.answer: Frescoes he commissioned at Santa Maria Antiqua in the Roman Forum survive, as do mosaic fragments from his oratory of the Virgin in Old St. Peter's, including a portrait of the pope.

faqs.question: How did John VII respond to the Quinisext canons?
faqs.answer: Justinian II asked him to approve the acceptable canons and reject the rest. According to the Liber Pontificalis, John simply sent them back without any changes.
